title: Per-vector + Batch-tier Pilot for Embeddings & Rerank — Contract/QSA Readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: run a controlled pilot that introduces a per-vector unit economics model for embeddings and a tiered batch-discount schedule for high-volume customers + ensure enterprise contract language and QSA artifacts are updated to reflect the new billing model.

Background: current embeddings pricing is single-rate/1000-vector equivalence and does not differentiate rerank flows or batching efficiencies. Customers have asked for clearer economics for large-scale retrieval and reranking use cases; finance needs a defensible pilot and legal/infosec need contract/QSA language that maps to the new units.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Introducing a per-vector unit with explicit rerank multipliers (candidate_count multiplier) improves predictability for customers doing large-scale reranking and reduces sticker shock vs naive per-embedding pricing.
- H2: A tiered batch-discount schedule (volume thresholds) will increase committed spend and smooth demand spikes without materially reducing unit economics when combined with auto-batching incentives.

Proposed pricing model (pilot):
- Unit definition: 1 vector-unit = 1 embedding vector (dimension-agnostic) evaluated at 1k-vector granularity for billing.
- Rerank multiplier: rerank_cost = base_vector_unit_price * candidate_multiplier where candidate_multiplier = 1 + floor((candidate_count - 1) / 50) * 0.25 up to 4x. (Example: 10 candidates -> multiplier 1.5)
- Batch-tier discounts (monthly usage):
  * Tier A: 0 – 499,999 vector-units => 1.00x (no discount)
  * Tier B: 500,000 – 4,999,999 => 0.87x (13% discount)
  * Tier C: 5,000,000+ => 0.72x (28% discount)
- Billing granularity: billed monthly. Rounding at 1000 vector-units.

Experiment design / pilot cohort:
- Cohort A (control): 1,000 customers randomly sampled from paid embeddings customers, billed under existing per-1000-vector rule.
- Cohort B (pilot): 1,000 customers matched by ARR and usage shape, billed under per-vector + tiered discounts.
- Duration: 8 weeks (2 week ramp, 6 week measurement).
- Primary metrics: net revenue per customer (NRPC), gross margin impact (finance modeled), churn/upgrade delta, customer-reported predictability score (survey).
- Secondary metrics: median invoice variance month-over-month, API request pattern changes (batching %), support ticket volume related to billing.

Telemetry & measurement plan:
- Events: embedding.create (vector_count), rerank.request (candidate_count, cached_prefix_hit boolean), billing.estimated_charge events emitted daily to experiments bucket.
- Dashboards: pilot-revenue, pilot-margin, pilot-churn; deck to be published weekly in Confluence.
- Statistical test: difference-in-difference on NRPC with 90% CI, uplift threshold 3%.

Contract & QSA readiness tasks:
- Update standard MSA and SOW language to include: clear definition of vector-unit, example invoice, and billing rounding rules. (Legal owner: Hannah Li)
- Produce a short QSA addendum explaining: telemetry data retained for billing reconciliation, encryption at rest for invoice metadata, and auditability of vector counts per customer (Infosec owner: Jason Park).
- Create approved template passages for sales to use in enterprise negotiations when customers request fixed-price/committed bundles.

Operational rollout steps:
1) Billing engine change (ENG): add vector-unit aggregation pipeline and tiered discount calculator behind feature flag (ENG-8421).
2) Console UI: show per-vector estimate and projected tier thresholds in billing preview (DES-284).
3) Contract/legal: add clauses + example invoice artifact to Drive (link below).
4) Pilot enablement: opt-in toggle for pilot cohort + support playbook.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: large customers with rerank-heavy workloads could see cost increases -> Mitigation: offer one-time grandfathered credits and a 30-day notice before billing change.
- Risk: billing reconciliation disputes -> Mitigation: provide daily per-customer usage exports and a 30-day reconciliation SLA with finance ops.
- Risk: QSA obligations unclear -> Mitigation: coordinate SOC2 owner and produce QSA addendum with signatures before pilot invoices issue.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Embeddings+PerVector+Pilot (internal)
- Finance model (read-only): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/pricing-models/pm-embeddings-per-vector-2026.xlsx
- Legal template drafts: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/legal/msas/embeddings-pilot-addendum.docx
- Experiment tracking ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PM-11789
- Billing engine implementation epic: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8421

Acceptance criteria:
- Billing engine can emit per-customer daily rollups (vector-units, rerank_multiplier applied) and compute monthly invoices behind the flag.
- Legal/QSA addendum reviewed and signed by Infosec owner and Legal.
- Pilot cohort created and customers notified; at least 80% of cohort have nonzero activity during the 6-week measurement window.
- Finance validates no more than 8% negative margin delta at company level in modeled outcomes for pilot sizes.
